title: Event Grid Topics, Events, and Subscriptions
description: Deep-dive into Event Grid topics, the event schema, and how subscriptions route events to handlers.

data.text: Every Event Grid event follows a consistent structure. The top-level properties identify the event, and the data property contains the payload specific to the event type. This predictable schema makes it easy to build generic handlers.

data.title: Standard Event Grid Event (JSON)
data.content: The envelope that wraps every event:

terms.definition: A publisher-defined path that describes what the event is about, such as orders/order-123.
A string identifying the kind of event, such as Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated.
The schema version of the data payload, used to handle breaking changes.
The resource path of the event source, used for routing and auditing.

data.text: Subscriptions control which events are delivered and where. You can filter by event type, subject prefix, subject suffix, or advanced rules based on event data fields. This prevents unwanted events from reaching your handlers.

data.title: Create an Event Subscription with Filters (Azure CLI)
data.content: Subscribe a webhook endpoint to only blob-created events in the uploads folder:
data.code:
az eventgrid event-subscription create \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --topic-name myCustomTopic \
  --name uploadHandler \
  --endpoint https://myapp.com/api/events \
  --included-event-types Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated \
  --subject-begins-with uploads/

rows: Events whose subject starts with a string
Events whose subject ends with a string

data.title: Keep Filters Specific
data.text: The more specific your filters, the fewer events you pay for. Event Grid pricing is per operation, so filtering at the subscription level reduces costs.

data.title: Design Event Subscriptions
data.description: A document management app publishes events for every file change. Design subscriptions for three teams.
steps: The image processing team needs only image files (.jpg, .png) in the photos folder.
The search indexing team needs all file changes in any folder.
The audit team needs all events for compliance logging.
data.expectedOutcome: Three event subscriptions with appropriate filters.
